notes:
Word counts now say whether they measured the page or the HTML behind it.

Some sites send their navigation, header and footer from the server but fetch
the article body with JavaScript afterwards. Docket reads the HTML as delivered,
so those pages looked almost empty: a developer platform was told at high
severity that fifteen pages "have almost no content" and offered the choice of
rewriting, merging or deleting them. Opened in a browser, the same pages carry
two hundred to six hundred words.

Nothing in the delivered HTML can settle which of the two it is, so Docket no
longer picks. The finding still reports what it measured — that count matters,
because the AI crawlers that do not run JavaScript see exactly what Docket saw —
but it now says the count is of the HTML as served, states that the pages were
not rendered, and tells you the remedy is the opposite one if the words are
there once JavaScript runs: server-render them, rather than write more. Sites
with no JavaScript framework are unaffected and keep the plain finding.

Separately, a duplicated title is now quoted the way the page writes it. A site
whose pages all say "GitLab" was shown "gitlab" in lower case, which is not a
string anyone could find in their own template.
